findings.title: The art bible's palette text no longer matches the regenerated palette
findings.claim: The bible still says the Art-ii pack palette brings the floors down to dark mid-tones, and the ramps table still lists electric as 'white, pale blue, violet'. The regenerated ROLE.floor is #bad2e0, a light blue about as light as the old #c7cfcc. The electric ramp is now #fffff0 #bad2e0 #6daec3 #565972 #3a3a50, with no violet: #7a367b mapped to the slate #565972.
findings.evidence: docs/art/bible.md:L31 ('Art-ii's pack palette brings floors down to dark mid-tones'), docs/art/bible.md:L43 (electric 'white, pale blue, violet'); diff L3839 (floor #bad2e0), diff L3889-L3895 (electric ramp). Neither bible line is in the Art-ii hunks (diff L1879, L1909).
findings.why: The bible is the rule page for the next pack (the new 'Adding a pack' section points there), and it now describes colours the palette does not have. A fresh clone's procedural floor is still light. Arcs and electric particles lose their violet hue, which the owner may want to see at the look gate.
findings.fix: Update bible L31: the paid Maru plating is dark, but the procedural floor role stays light (#bad2e0). Update the electric row of the ramps table to the mapped steps, or add an `electric` override in art/palette-overrides.json if the owner wants violet back (#6c70a4 or #bea8d5 are in the palette).

findings.title: The callout lift per player (liftFor) has no test
findings.claim: callouts.ts picks the callout lift per player: Puny 0.6 tile, LimeZu standing 64, LimeZu downed or dead 26, and Puny whenever `crew` or `crewArt` is missing. No test drives createCalloutLayer to check it. crewArt.test.ts only checks the constants and bubbleAnchor's `lift` parameter.
findings.evidence: diff L3124-L3131 (liftFor), diff L3150 (its use); tests/crewArt.test.ts at diff L4429-L4434 (only bubbleAnchor with an explicit lift); progress.md L302 (the Task 2 minor 'liftFor untested').
findings.why: A wrong feature check or downed check here (for example, the bubble left at 19.2 units, inside a LimeZu head, or a downed bubble floating 64 units over an empty tile) passes the suite. Plan Decision 6 promises this behaviour.
findings.fix: Add one test that builds createCalloutLayer with the fakeAssets from crewArt.test.ts, with and without crewArt. Draw one bubble for a conscious player and one for a downed player, then check each root.y against bubbleAnchor(..., CALLOUT_LIFT_LIMEZU / CALLOUT_LIFT_DOWN_LIMEZU / CALLOUT_LIFT_PUNY).y - 20 - TAIL.

findings.title: The palette builder reads frames without the importer's bounds check
findings.claim: countColours indexes `img.data` for every frame rectangle without checking that it fits the pack image. A rectangle past the edge reads undefined: `undefined < 128` is false, so the pixel counts as colour 0 (black) and can drag a k-means centre. runImport reports the same mistake as a problem, but art:palette runs before art:import. Related: an index override past a ramp's length leaves a sparse array (undefined goes into toHex), and tidyRamp throws on an empty ramp.
findings.evidence: diff L2872-L2877 (no bounds check); scripts/art/importCore.ts:L134 (the importer's 'rectangle ... is outside' check); diff L2952 (index override), diff L2930-L2933 (tidyRamp on an empty list reads out[-1]); progress.md L301.
findings.why: The committed config and overrides avoid all three cases, so today's palette is right. But the new 'Adding a pack' flow tells the owner to run art:palette right after editing art/import.json, and a typo there silently changes the palette instead of failing with a message.
findings.fix: In countColours, throw `art:palette: rectangle x,y wxh is outside <pack> (WxH)` when f.x + f.w > img.width or f.y + f.h > img.height, mirroring importCore.ts:L134. In mapRoles, reject an index override >= the ramp's length. Add one test for the out-of-bounds frame.

Downed: stand.s, anchor 0.5/0.5, +pi/2, alpha 0.85. Dead: grey and opaque. Consoles: STATION_IDS order matches the StationKind numbers (stationKinds.ts:L2-L4). consoleArtName uses the group's first member. SIDE_ROTATION n 0, e +pi/2, s pi, w -pi/2 turns the south-facing art into the room. consolePlacement backs onto the desk's outer edge (WALL_GAP = 10, consoleModel.ts:L20, even), is centred along the wall, floors the top-left to even units, and swaps the box for e/w (diff L3257-L3266; test L4250-L4265). The sprites go in a child container at index 0, under `g` and the feel's fixtures added later (consoleLayer L3180-L3181, renderer.ts L3948, interiorView.ts:L64). Tints are 0xffffff, 0xcccccc and 0x999999. Redraws happen only on a look or layout key (L3187-L3188). The one-frame console outputs in art/import.json:L1750-L1840 match the spec's rectangles.

Blasts: one room blast per hit room at roomCentroid, rounded to even units. The duel's blast goes on the smoke's tile. One spark per breach opening at the siteTile centre. Cap 4 is shared and cuts the oldest (addBlast). The frame comes from clock.t after advance, so it holds through the hitstop and at dt 0 (interiorFeel.ts:L161-L163). Blasts are removed after the last frame and cleared on reset() and build() (diff L3649/L3732). They sit in `above`, under the flash. renderer.reset() calls feel.reset() on a new run (renderer.ts:L89), so no blast leaks across runs.

Palette builder: farthest-point start weighted by ln(1 + count), with ties to the earlier colour (strict >) in (count desc, RGB asc) order. Kept colours seed `near` but are never centres. Up to 12 Lloyd iterations snap to member colours, an empty cluster keeps its centre, and the loop stops early. The output is sorted by OKLab L then RGB. Ramps are tidied and padded to 5. An override colour not in the palette fails the build. Output is JSON.stringify(…, 2) plus a newline, deterministic (diff L2862-L2975). A frame counted twice is counted once, and the console rectangles in art/import.json:L1754-L1835 equal the existing cuts at L39-L97, so the palette is unchanged by them (Decision 2).

palette.json: 48 colours, and every role and ramp colour is in `colours` (checked by hand against diff L3760-L3902).
